eligibility_reason: Section 2.2 (p. 4) equips the speculator with three online memory systems — a contrastive transition table, an episodic memory, and a confusion tracker — that accumulate from past agent trajectories at run time and are queried on later episodes/tasks to condition the speculator's own future predictions. The abstract and p. 1 state that gains 'grow continuously as memory accumulates' as more episodes are completed, i.e. state written in one episode conditions behaviour in later ones, satisfying I1. Published 2026 (I2), English (I3), and full text was retrievable (I4). None of E1–E7 apply: the memory captures action-sequence statistics, retrieved trajectory segments, and recurring-error patterns with explicit cross-episode semantics rather than being a stateless inference/cache optimisation (not E1, p. 1: 'existing speculators are stateless and discard all information between tasks'); an externalised store exists beyond the parametric speculator model (not E2); the stores are written online by the system itself, not fixed (not E3, p. 4); this is primary research with benchmark results, not a review (not E4); memory is the paper's central, title-level contribution (not E5); the system is an LLM-based agent pipeline (actor + LLM speculator) (not E6); and the paper is a full 21-page submission (not E7).

facets.justification: Section 2.2 (p. 4): the episodic memory embeds the current context with OpenAI's text-embedding-3-small (1536 dim) and retrieves the top-k most similar past episodes via cosine similarity — an embedding store the speculator itself writes online from trajectories. This is the component present in every benchmark's best-performing configuration in Table 7 (p. 19: Epi+Miss, Episodic, or the full Memory setting). The other two stores (contrastive transition table, confusion tracker) serve different purposes — aggregate action statistics and error suppression — and are not fused with episodic retrieval via any declared ranking rule (p. 4), so per the guide's 'different purposes, not multi_store' boundary they are recorded as secondary rather than coded as a combined substrate.

p. 4: completed episodes are stored as new trajectory segments (context, actions, observation, arg_sources, outcome, lesson); the 'lesson' field is 'auto-generated from episode metadata via template rules' and 'all episode fields are constructed by rule-based heuristics without auxiliary LLM calls' — which rules out reflect_synthesize, since no model-generated higher-level content is produced. No text on pp. 1, 2, 4, 9, 17, 19–20 describes existing episodic entries being rewritten, merged or deleted, ruling out edit_in_place.
p. 4: 'the current context is embedded ... and the top-k most similar episodes are retrieved via cosine similarity, providing the speculator with structured examples of similar past situations.'

Evaluated by replay against six public benchmarks (WebArena, ALFWorld, VWA, PDDL, τ²-bench, HotpotQA) against a Stateless baseline with significance testing (Table 7, p. 19). Appendix B.4 (p. 19) states directly: 'Our replay-based design evaluates speculation accuracy in isolation ... A live deployment study incorporating real API latencies is necessary to measure true end-to-end wall-clock savings and validate that the accuracy measured during replay translates to a proportional speedup in practice' — confirming no deployed, real-stakes setting was studied, only controlled benchmark comparison. Coded conservatively per the guide's validation/evaluation boundary.

Section 4 (p. 9) and Table 7 (p. 19): seven progressive memory settings are run across six fixed benchmark suites, reporting accuracy and latency-reduction scores against a Stateless baseline, with McNemar's-test significance per benchmark.

Contributions list, p. 2: 'We augment speculative execution for LLM agents with three complementary memory systems that accumulate experience from past trajectories: a contrastive transition table, an episodic memory with miss-episode recording, and a confusion tracker.' This is framed as a technique/algorithm augmenting an existing pipeline; none of the given pages describe a released tool or artefact as the thing being argued for.
